public_payload.normalized_proposition: GPT-4 does not solve any of the core truthfulness and reliability problems identified in Marcus's March 2022 essay.

statement.excerpt: It doesn’t actually solve any of the core problems of truthfulness and reliability that I laid out in my infamous March 2022 essay Deep Learning is Hitting a Wall.

from_speaker: core problems of truthfulness and reliability
March 2022 essay Deep Learning is Hitting a Wall
our_interpretation: Solve means provide dependable performance on a problem class, rather than merely improve an average benchmark score. It does not require mathematical perfection.
The referenced essay supplies the scope: factual trustworthiness, reasoning and common sense, and robustness on unfamiliar or outlying inputs.
The word any makes the statement broader than the narrower claim that some hallucinations and reasoning failures remain.
The original model's launch-to-post state is the latest public snapshot appropriate to this ongoing observation.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence mapped to the referenced core problem classes shows that each remained materially unresolved in the original GPT-4.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Appropriate evaluations establish that the original GPT-4 dependably solved at least one of those core problem classes.

evidence.excerpt: Most importantly, it still is not fully reliable (it “hallucinates” facts and makes reasoning errors).
evidence.explanation: OpenAI directly acknowledges continuing factual and reasoning failures, supporting those parts of the claim. The same section reports a 40% improvement over its latest GPT-3.5 on internal adversarial factuality evaluations, which limits any reading that no progress occurred.

evidence.excerpt: Deep-learning systems are particularly problematic when it comes to “outliers” that differ substantially from the things on which they are trained.
evidence.locator: Discussion of high-stakes applications and outliers
evidence.explanation: This establishes that the referenced scope includes robustness beyond familiar training examples. It is Marcus's own writing and is used only to define scope, never as outcome evidence.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A defensible mapping of the referenced core problems to evaluations of the launch model, with evidence of whether each problem class remained materially unresolved.
